title: Multiple color themes with data-theme
when: The user wants several themes (light, dark, high contrast, seasonal or brand variants) that visitors can pick.
prompt:
Goal: Themes as token overrides on [data-theme] values, switchable at runtime, remembered, and each passing contrast.
Steps:
1. Keep one set of semantic token names; each theme only reassigns them: [data-theme="dark"] { --color-bg: #15161a; --color-text: #e8e6e3 }.
2. With no saved choice follow the system with a prefers-color-scheme: dark block; a choice sets data-theme on the html element.
3. Add a high contrast theme (text 15 to 1 or more, visible borders, no shadows) and leave forced-colors mode alone.
4. Build the picker as a labeled select or radio group (System, Light, Dark, High contrast), not unlabeled color dots.
5. Save the choice in localStorage inside try and catch, and apply it from a tiny head script before first paint to avoid a flash.
6. Set color-scheme per theme so native controls follow.
Quality bar:
- Every theme passes 4.5 to 1 for text.
- Switching needs no reload.
- Charts and images stay legible in each theme.
Pitfalls:
- A duplicated stylesheet per theme.
- Blocked storage in private mode breaking the page.
- A light flash before the saved theme applies.
Verify:
- [ ] Theme blocks only override tokens.
- [ ] A dark theme exists.
- [ ] The picker has a label.
- [ ] Storage access is guarded.
Output: Theme blocks in tokens.css or style.css and theme.js for the picker.

examples.input: let users pick light, dark or high contrast
examples.output: select with System, Light, Dark, High contrast; [data-theme] token overrides; choice saved with try and catch
